extracted.intended_audience: Authors, editors, reviewers, and readers of qualitative research (especially in health professions and medical education)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards for reporting qualitative research to improve transparency across paradigms, approaches, and methods; intended to guide manuscript preparation, peer review, and critical appraisal. The SRQR comprises 21 items describing what information should be included in a qualitative research report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: Concise description of the nature and topic of the study; identifying the study as qualitative or indicating the approach (e.g., ethnography, grounded theory) or data collection methods (e.g., interview, focus group) is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make title explicit about qualitative nature or approach to help readers identify study type and method. Keep concise and topic-focused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary of key elements of the study using the abstract format of the intended publication; typically includes background, purpose, methods, results, and conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report key elements clearly; results in qualitative abstracts are narrative rather than numerical. Include enough methods and findings detail for readers to judge relevance and trustworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem formulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Description and significance of the problem/phenomenon studied; review of relevant theory and empirical work; problem statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the problem matters and situate it in existing literature and theory. Clarify conceptual background that shaped research questions and approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose or research question
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose of the study and specific objectives or questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clear aims or research questions (qualitative studies typically explore 'how?' and 'why?' questions). Ensure purpose aligns with chosen approach and guides methods and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative approach and research paradigm
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative approach (e.g., ethnography, grounded theory, case study, phenomenology, narrative research) and guiding theory if appropriate; identifying the research paradigm (e.g., postpositivist, constructivist/interpretivist) is also recommended; rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe and justify the chosen approach and paradigm rather than merely naming it. The rationale should explain why this theory/approach/method was chosen over alternatives, the assumptions and limitations implicit in that choice, and how choices influence conclusions and transferability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher characteristics and reflexivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers’ characteristics that may influence the research, including personal attributes, qualifications/experience, relationship with participants, assumptions, and/or presuppositions; potential or actual interaction between researchers’ characteristics and the research questions, approach, methods, results, and/or transferability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report reflexivity: how researchers’ backgrounds, relationships, and perspectives may have influenced data collection and interpretation. Describe who was involved in data collection/analysis and how their roles shaped findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting/site and salient contextual factors; rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the setting and important contextual features that bear on interpretation and transferability. Explain why that context was relevant to the research question and findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: How and why research participants, documents, or events were selected; criteria for deciding when no further sampling was necessary (e.g., sampling saturation); rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain inclusion/exclusion criteria, sampling procedures (purposive, theoretical, convenience, etc.), recruitment processes, and stopping rules (e.g., how saturation was defined and recognized). Justify sampling choices relative to study aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical issues pertaining to human subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation of approval by an appropriate ethics review board and participant consent, or explanation for lack thereof; other confidentiality and data security issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report IRB/ethics approval, consent procedures, steps taken to protect confidentiality and data security, and any ethical concerns particular to the study design or participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of data collected; details of data collection procedures including (as appropriate) start and stop dates of data collection and analysis, iterative process, triangulation of sources/methods, and modification of procedures in response to evolving study findings; rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how data were collected in sufficient detail (e.g., timing, iterative cycles, triangulation), and any adaptations made during the study. Avoid merely naming methods without explaining how they were implemented (e.g., how 'saturation' or 'iteration' was operationalized).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection instruments and technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of instruments (e.g., interview guides, questionnaires) and devices (e.g., audio recorders) used for data collection; if/how the instrument(s) changed over the course of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples or appendices of instruments where possible and explain any revisions made during data collection and why. Report technical details relevant to data capture and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units of study
rubrics_metrics.description: Number and relevant characteristics of participants, documents, or events included in the study; level of participation (could be reported in results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sample size and participant characteristics (demographics, roles), and indicate participation rates or attrition. Make clear what constituted a unit of analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for processing data prior to and during analysis, including transcription, data entry, data management and security, verification of data integrity, data coding, and anonymization/deidentification of excerpts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe procedures for preparing raw data for analysis (transcription conventions, storage, coding software, quality checks) and measures taken to protect data integrity and participant anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Process by which inferences, themes, etc., were identified and developed, including the researchers involved in data analysis; usually references a specific paradigm or approach; rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain analytic steps (coding approaches, theme development, use of constant comparison, matrix analysis, etc.), who conducted analyses, how disagreements were resolved, and how analytic decisions were grounded in data and/or theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Techniques to enhance trustworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques to enhance trustworthiness and credibility of data analysis (e.g., member checking, audit trail, triangulation); rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report methods used to increase credibility, dependability, confirmability, and transferability (for example, member checking, triangulation, multiple coders, audit trails), and explain why chosen techniques were appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Main findings (e.g., interpretations, inferences, and themes); might include development of a theory or model, or integration with prior research or theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present main analytic findings clearly, describing patterns, themes, or models that emerged. Provide interpretive narrative that connects findings to research questions and analytic approach rather than just descriptive summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Links to empirical data
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence (e.g., quotes, field notes, text excerpts, photographs) to substantiate analytic findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sufficient illustrative data excerpts (participant quotes, observations) to support interpretations and allow readers to judge plausibility. Indicate source and context of excerpts and anonymize as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration with prior work, implications, transferability, and contribution(s) to the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Short summary of main findings; explanation of how findings and conclusions connect to, support, elaborate on, or challenge conclusions of earlier scholarship; discussion of scope of application/generalizability; identification of unique contribution(s) to scholarship in a discipline or field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how results relate to existing literature and theory, implications for practice or policy, and considerations for transferability to other contexts. Identify the study's unique contributions and the boundaries of applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Trustworthiness and limitations of findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss potential threats to credibility and the limits of interpretation (sampling limitations, researcher influence, contextual constraints). Be explicit about uncertainties and how they affect conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential sources of influence or perceived influence on study conduct and conclusions; how these were managed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose financial, professional, or personal interests that could affect study conduct or interpretation, and describe steps taken to manage or mitigate those influences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources of funding and other support; role of funders in data collection, interpretation, and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report funding sources and any supports (grants, institutional resources) and clarify the funders’ roles (if any) in study design, data collection, analysis, interpretation, or manuscript preparation.
